messages:
Marta: Quick follow-up to the kernel-selection + attention-opt RFC — we need a clear migration plan for per-model kernel feature state. Right now flags are a blob in runtime DB under `kernel_flags`. I propose we move to a small service (call it `model_feature_state`) that owns per-model enablement, supports atomic updates, and keeps an audit trail. Goal: eliminate transient double-toggles during canary flips and provide an easy rollback path.

Jia: Agreed. Service-backed state sounds right. Migration approach idea: a one-shot reconcile job that reads the old `kernel_flags` map and writes entries into the new service only if no state already exists there. That avoids stomping any manual changes and prevents write storms during rollout. Migration job should be idempotent and emit a CSV/dry-run.

Samir: Important compatibility note: different kernels have incompatible KV cache blob formats. If we switch kernels mid-session we risk cache poisoning. Two mitigations: 1) namespace cache keys by kernel version so old blobs aren't reused, or 2) run a compatibility shim that can translate blobs (expensive). I prefer the namespace approach + explicit invalidation when kernel changes.

Kevin: Namespace by kernel version makes sense. Example key format:```cache_key = f\"model:{model_id}:kernel_v{kernel_version}:{prefix_hash}\``` Also we should emit a `kernel_migrate` telemetry event with fields old_kernel/new_kernel/reason so we can alert on migrations.

deploy-bot: infra-canary: scheduled canary deploy to group `canary-runtime` 2026-03-22 02:00 UTC.

Marta: Migration job pseudocode (idempotent):```for model in all_models:
  old_val = runtime_db.get('kernel_flags').get(model)
  if not new_service.exists(model):
    new_service.write(model, {'kernel': old_val, 'migrated_at': now()})
  else:
    # leave already-migrated models alone
    continue```Make sure the job records progress and supports resume.

Jia: Also need a global kill-switch per cluster plus per-model fallback chains. Runtime should be able to consult a `fallback_chain` array such as `["fast-quant", "standard", "cpu-fallback"]` and pick the first compatible kernel. That avoids operators manually flipping things during incidents.

Samir: Operational edge case: a single batched request that references multiple models with different kernel pins. Runtime must not mix kernels in one batch. Options: split the batch by kernel (correctness, higher latency) or fall back the whole batch to a safe common kernel. I prefer splitting batches and tracking split counts.

Kevin: I'll add telemetry counters for `batch_split_count` and `kernel_migration_count`. We should surface a console chart for both and an alert on abnormal growth. Also add a health probe that reports fallback rate and kernel mismatch rejections.

Marta: Action items and owners:
- migration job (reconcile + write + dry-run CSV): @Jia
- cache key namespacing + invalidation tooling: @Samir
- telemetry events, dashboard, alerts, and console UI for per-model state: @Kevin
- canary plan docs and cluster kill-switch procedures: @Marta

Marta: Canary safety thresholds: abort canary if error-rate delta > 0.5% or avg token latency increase > 20% for the canary cohort vs baseline. Create an alert `kernel_migration_regression`.

Jia: ETA for migration job: 2 weeks. Will include dry-run mode and a CSV of intended writes. Will also include a mode to mark models as \"migrated_manually\" so we don't overwrite hand-edits.

Samir: I'll prototype the key prefix + an invalidation script and validate with a tiny model canary. Will also add unit tests to ensure old blobs aren't accidentally read.

Kevin: I'll wire up telemetry and console bits. Will add the health probe and the alert rule for fallback frequency.

Marta: One more operational note — batched RPCs crossing kernel boundaries: log the split decision and emit a `batch_split_reason` tag so SRE can correlate latency spikes.

Jia: For the new `model_feature_state` service API, suggest endpoints: `GET /models/:id/state`, `POST /models/:id/state` (atomic), `POST /migrations/dryrun`, `GET /migrations/:id/status`. Keep the model state minimal: `{ 'kernel': 'fast-quant', 'migrated_at': ts, 'source': 'migration|manual' }`.

Samir: For cache invalidation, we should provide an async job that scans recently-migrated models and invalidates keys by prefix. That job should be safe to run repeatedly.

Kevin: I'll add a dashboard alert on `kernel_migrate` events that exceed a baseline rate, and a PagerDuty escalation if migration error-rate > 0.5%.

Marta: OK — sync Monday 10:00am PST to review canary checklist, rollback steps, and migration dry-run output. Please drop the dry-run CSV to `s3://redwood-migrations/migration-dryruns/` and link in the meeting notes. :thumbsup:
